description: VYNTARA is an independent participant team taking part in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. With an interest in science, space exploration, environmental sustainability and innovation, I aim to explore real-world challenges using NASA's open data and develop a creative, meaningful solution. Driven by curiosity, learning and a passion for discovery.
summary: Earth System Trend Detective explores how Earth's climate system is changing by analysing four important environmental indicators: global surface temperature, atmospheric carbon dioxide, Arctic sea ice extent, and global sea-level rise. Using NASA datasets and partner scientific records, we examine long-term trends, compare independent observations, and identify patterns in Earth's changing climate. Our analysis reveals accelerated global warming, rising atmospheric CO₂ concentrations, declining Arctic winter sea ice, and increasing sea levels. We also propose an Earth Vital Signs dashboard that brings these indicators together in one accessible visual platform. VYNTARA aims to make complex Earth science data easier to understand and encourage informed environmental awareness through evidence-based analysis.
details:
VYNTARA is an Earth System Trend Detective project that investigates changes in Earth's climate using four independent environmental indicators: global surface temperature, atmospheric CO₂ concentration, Arctic sea ice extent, and global mean sea level.

The project uses NASA GISS GISTEMP v4 temperature records, NOAA Mauna Loa CO₂ measurements, NASA/NSIDC Arctic sea ice observations, and NASA/CNES satellite altimetry data.

We analyze long-term temperature and CO₂ records using statistical methods, including linear regression, trend comparison, and correlation analysis. Published NASA and NSIDC observations are used to examine Arctic sea ice and sea-level changes.

Our findings are presented through warming stripes, trend visualizations, statistical comparisons, and a proposed Earth Vital Signs dashboard.

The creative aspect of VYNTARA is its integration of four different Earth-system indicators into one understandable visual story. The project aims to improve climate awareness, communicate scientific evidence, and demonstrate how open Earth observation data can help people understand our changing planet.

The dashboard is currently a conceptual mock-up, with future plans for automated data updates and location-based exploration.
